                                         1. Introduction                                                     tion significantly constrains their applicability in real-world
                                                                                                             dynamic environments.
                                         Vision-language models (VLMs) have made remarkable
                                         progress on tasks such as image captioning and visual ques-            In contrast to standard frame-based cameras, event cam-
                                         tion answering (VQA), demonstrating a strong ability to             eras provide a complementary modality. Instead of cap-
                                         interpret and describe visual scenes [1, 4, 21]. However,           turing full image frames at fixed rates, an event camera
                                         most existing VLMs rely on high-quality RGB images and              asynchronously records per-pixel brightness changes with
                                                                                                             microsecond-level latency and high dynamic range [9]. This
                                           * Equal contribution.                                             unique mechanism preserves fast motion cues while avoid-

Figure 2. Construction of RE-VLM: data generation pipeline and model. Left: A graph-driven pipeline converts synchronized RGB
frames and event streams into a graph, extracts verifiable scene facts, and synthesizes reliable caption and QA supervision. Center:
Representative examples from the datasets yielded by the pipeline: PEOD-Chat (illumination-challenged scenes) and RGBE-Chat (general
scenarios). Right: The RE-VLM model fuses static RGB appearance features with dynamic cues from events and is trained with a progressive
strategy for robust captioning and VQA under low-light, high-dynamic-range, and fast-motion conditions.

Figure 3. Data generation pipeline overview. From reconstructed event frames and RGB images, two modality-specific graphs are
constructed. A degradation-aware fusion then merges them into a single RGB-event graph (nodes: entities, edges: relations). Finally, captions
and VQA items are synthesized from the fused graph. (S: subject, P: place, D: direction, T: target; H: hierarchical relation; A: attribute.)

Figure 4. RE-VLM model architecture. Synchronized RGB and event streams are encoded. During training, a Spatio-Temporal Alignment
Module (STAM) provides alignment signals and a relation loss. During inference, event features after the temporal DWConv are projected
(event adapter) and, together with RGB tokens (RGB adapter), are fed to the LLM.

ment regularizer is defined as the average of these weighted            dual-branch representation.

Temporal Alignment Module (STAM). On both benchmarks,
using only RGB or only event data still yields reasonable cap-                                 6. Conclusion
tioning and VQA performance. The joint RGB+Event config-
uration consistently outperforms either single-modality set-                                   We introduced RE-VLM, a dual-stream vision–language
ting, demonstrating that our dual-branch architecture effec-                                   model that jointly leverages RGB images and event streams
tively exploits the complementary information from events                                      for robust scene understanding. To address the scarcity of
and RGB, especially under adverse conditions. We also ex-                                      RGB-Event-Text supervision, we further introduced a graph-
amine the contribution of the STAM module by comparing                                         driven data generation pipeline and constructed two datasets
against a variant that replaces STAM with naive feature con-                                   covering both common and challenging conditions. Experi-
catenation. Incorporating STAM leads to consistent improve-                                    ments show that RE-VLM consistently outperforms strong
ments or maintenance of performance across both datasets.                                      RGB-only and event-only baselines, particularly in challeng-
Cross-Validation with an Open-Source LLM Judge. Be-                                            ing scenarios, providing a practical foundation for future
cause GPT-3.5-Turbo is closed-source, and following recent                                     work on event-augmented vision-language understanding.
